## Summary

Implemented Task 5 (the `resolve_call_site_full` integration) of the scope-graph precision-recovery plan, exactly as specified, plus one necessary deviation to satisfy the task's own "no regressions" requirement.

### Files modified
- `src/resolution.rs` (+201/-3 lines)
- `tests/integration/resolution_test.rs` (+314 lines)

### Implementation (per plan, verbatim)
- Rewrote the Rust scope branch of `resolve_call_site_full` (~line 787): splits an owner-keyed `::` name via the new `owner_method_key` helper, gates on `has_bare_pool`, diverts free-function misroutes via `rust_graph_qualified_target_is_free_fn`, and drives owner-method sites through `rust_scope_prune_owner` (the `ScopeResolution` disproof prune) with fail-open to `owner_lookup_in_modules`.
- Added `rust_graph_qualified_target_is_free_fn`, `rust_scope_prune_owner`, and `owner_method_key` exactly as the plan's code blocks specify.
- Added the 7 plan-specified tests to `tests/integration/resolution_test.rs`.

### RED → GREEN evidence
Ran `cargo test --test integration resolution_test::scope_graph_` before implementing: 2 passed (regression pins), 5 failed exactly as the plan predicted (drop vs demote, keep-all vs wrong-prune). After implementing: all 7 passed. Verified the free-fn guard actually fires by temporarily disabling it (`&& false`) — `scope_graph_free_fn_path_not_misrouted_to_colliding_method_pool` then failed by resolving to the wrong cross-module method file (`src/other.rs` instead of `src/m.rs`); restored, it passed again.

### Three drop-invariant re-confirmation
`rust_scope_graph_unqualified_declines_do_not_legacy_guess`, `rust_scope_graph_qualified_paths_resolve_or_disable_legacy_stem`, `rust_scope_graph_authority_gate_and_poison_skip_legacy` — all pass. Full `resolution_test::` suite: 131 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

### Deviation from the plan (found via full-suite run, fixed within Task 5's own file)
`cargo test` (full suite) surfaced one regression outside the plan's named tests: `tests/ast/cpg_test.rs::cha_upgrades_graph_resolved_owner_pair_to_exact` (pre-existing, passing before my change — confirmed via `git stash`). Root cause: `self.methods` keys owner-method pools by **trait name** too (not just concrete struct/enum owners), via pre-existing `trait_key` population in `call_graph.rs`. For `Render::draw(x)` (calling a trait method through the trait name — true dynamic/vtable dispatch, no static callee), the bare pool `("Render","draw")` collides across `A::draw`/`B::draw`. `②B`/`①C` pass cleanly (no shadow, direct binding), but the resolved graph target is the trait's own bodyless declaration, whose `graph_target_ids` is empty — so the predicate disproves nothing, `rust_scope_prune_owner` returns "unchanged," and the plan's literal fail-open routes it to `owner_lookup_in_modules`, reviving the legacy `TraitCha` demotion that an earlier (#120) invariant test requires disabled for authoritative sites (that fan-out is supposed to come solely from the CPG's separate CHA-enrichment step, seeded from real `Exact` edges).

Fix (confined to `src/resolution.rs`, no other files/tasks touched): before falling through to the `owner_lookup_in_modules` fail-open, check whether the qualified path resolved to a *definite* graph target whose id-set is empty — if so, this isn't "uncertain" (the ①C/②B fail-open's intended trigger), it's the same decline `rust_scope_graph_resolution` already treats as a drop, so it drops instead of fail-opening. Verified this doesn't affect any of the 7 new tests or the 3 invariants (all still green) since it only fires when the callable edge resolves to `Some` target with an empty id-set — none of the plan's own test fixtures hit that combination.

### Verified
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo test` (full suite, all 27 test binaries + lib + main unittests): **2372 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored** across every binary (cli included, no stall on this run).
- `cargo build --release` + `cd eval && uv run tier-a --matrix-only --allow-stale-sut`: all Rust fixtures `ok`, including `rust/trait_dyn_dispatch` (exit 0, no regressions/mismatches).
- Manually confirmed the previously-regressed `cha_upgrades_graph_resolved_owner_pair_to_exact` now passes, and that it genuinely failed before my fix (not vacuously).

### Not verified
- Did not run `uv run tier-a --quick` (needs rust-analyzer, minutes-long) or `--corpus all` (human-triggered per `eval/README.md`) — out of scope for this task per the instructions ("Do NOT touch eval/" and Task 5 doesn't call for the quick/full harness).
- Did not run Tasks 7/8 (recovery counter, further Tier-A gating) — explicitly out of scope.
- Did not commit — edits are left uncommitted per instructions for the host to commit.
